newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says petroleum year profit rises.
newsitem.headline: BHP says petroleum year profit rises.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Thursday its petroleum division recorded an annual profit including abnormal items to May 31, 1997 of A$676 million, up 105.5 percent on last year's A$329 million profit.
Excluding abnormal items, the profit was a record A$693 million, up A$274 million, or 65.4 percent, on last year.
BHP said the result was affected by a higher average realised oil price, increased profits from the sale of petroleum properties, the asset write-off of Dai Hung and increased exploration activity.
The average realised oil price was A$28.27 per barrel, compared with A$24.80 last year, reflecting higher U.S. dollar prices, partly offset by a stronger Australian dollar.
The sale of significant petroleum properties raised A$96 million after tax, compared with a loss of A$11 million last year, net of a write-down of Wyoming assets of A$24 million.
BHP said exploration expenditure was A$418 million, against A$325 million last year, of which A$328 million, against A$221 million, was charged to profit.
The after-tax exploration expense benfited from the tax effecting of certain prior years overseas exploration expenditure.
BHP said an abnormal loss of A$124 million represented a write-down of refinery assets.
This was partly offset by an abnormal profit of A$107 million following settlement of the Petroleum Resource Rent Tax issue with the Victorian government.
The division had a net abnormal loss of A$90 million last year.
The division paid income tax of A$438 million, excluding abnormal items, representing an effective tax rate of 38.7 percent, against 44.1 percent last year.

This exceeded the nominal Australian rate of 36 percent due to the effect of non-deductible accounting amortisation and exploration expenditure, partly offset by the recognition of a tax benefit on some exploration expenditure and prior year over provisions.
